name: Crab scratch
lesson:
## Four fingers, four clicks, one stroke

A one-beat forward stroke with four rapid fader clicks across it, then a silent one-beat return; once a bar for 4 bars. The clicks come from the four fingers of the fader hand hitting the fader in turn against the thumb, which springs it back: eight fader moves in a beat, about 40 ms apart at this tempo.

The crab is the fastest thing a fader can do, and Wikipedia's description is right that it is a finger technique, not a wrist one. Set the crossfader curve as sharp as it goes and the cut lag to zero. The scorer counts eight moves in the beat; if you can only get three fingers to fire, the pattern still lands but the count will show it.
